_meta.description: Deep-time validation anchors: published paleontological / cyclostratigraphic measurements vs the model's deep-time chain (Phase 19 dossier; plan 12 option A). OBSERVED values are verbatim from the cited sources; the model predictions are NOT stored here — tools/verify/paleo-anchors.js recomputes them live from the engine and asserts each expectation. Since plan 12 (option A) the Earth–Moon distance history is a CITED PHYSICAL INPUT (data/astrogeo22-earth-moon.json — Farhat et al. 2022) and nothing in the chain is fitted to these rows: every row is a TEST of the derived day length, distance and composed precession. Documented deviations are encoded as deviation BANDS: the gate fails on an unexplained IMPROVEMENT too (verify-laws precedent — a suddenly-matching miss means the formula or the input changed). Each band names its cause in `note`.

recipes.lodHr: meanLodSecondsAtAge(ageMa) / 3600 — angular-momentum conservation on the cited distance history, L_EM the J2000 constant
recipes.moonDistanceRE: meanMoonDistanceCorrectedAtAge(ageMa) / earthParallaxRadiusKm (raw meanMoonDistanceAtAge for the moonDistanceRawRE rows — the solar-Δa correction is a modern-orbit construct)
recipes.precArcsecPerYr: meanLunisolarPrecessionRateArcsecPerYrAtAge(ageMa) — the COMPOSED lunisolar rate [ω(t)/ω₀]·p₀·[f_S + (1 − f_S)(a₀/a_M(t))³] on the derived LOD and the cited distance (@essrt/physics/earth/precession-composed; falsification leg 1, plan 06 D6/Phase 3).

expectationTypes.range: predicted inside [lo, hi], allowing outsideToleranceAbs beyond either edge
expectationTypes.deviationBandPct: (predicted/observed - 1) * 100 inside band [lo, hi] — a DOCUMENTED deviation that must persist
expectationTypes.deviationBandOutsideRange: signed distance outside the observed range (positive above hi, negative below lo) inside band [lo, hi]

sources.wells1963: Wells, J.W. 1963. Coral growth and geochronometry. Nature 197, 948–950 (table via Arbab 2001 review)
sources.winter2020: de Winter et al. 2020. Subdaily-scale chemical variability in a Torreites sanchezi rudist shell. Paleoceanography and Paleoclimatology 35, e2019PA003723
sources.pannella1972: Pannella 1972 / Scrutton — bivalve growth increments, ~90 Ma
sources.williams2000: Williams, G.E. 2000. Geological constraints on the Precambrian history of Earth's rotation. Rev. Geophys. 38, 37–59 (Elatina tidal rhythmites)
sources.mitchellKirscher2023: Mitchell, R.N. & Kirscher, U. 2023. Mid-Proterozoic day length stalled by tidal resonance. Nature Geoscience 16, 567–569
sources.wu2024: Wu, Malinverno, Meyers, et al. 2024. A 650-Myr history of Earth's axial precession frequency... Science Advances, doi:10.1126/sciadv.ado2412
sources.farhat2022: Farhat, Auclair-Desrotour, Boué & Laskar 2022. The resonant tidal evolution of the Earth-Moon distance. A&A 665, L1 (arXiv 2207.00438). Proxy compilation (Weeli Wolli tidal rhythmites, Moodies Group tidal bundles) — and, since plan 12 option A, the model's cited distance INPUT (AstroGeo22; data/astrogeo22-earth-moon.json). A row that compares the derived chain with that input's own proxies tests the derivation, not the input.
sources.zhou2024: Zhou et al. 2024. Earth-Moon dynamics from cyclostratigraphy reveals possible ocean tide resonance in the Mesoproterozoic era. Science Advances, doi:10.1126/sciadv.adn7674 — the MEASURED quantity per formation is the precession constant k (1σ); the paper's Earth–Moon distance and length of day are DERIVED from k 'using online tools provided by the AstroGeo Project (Farhat et al. 2022)', assuming conservation of angular momentum (Chuanlinggou/Wumishan/Yemahe)
sources.meyersMalinverno2018: Meyers & Malinverno 2018. Proterozoic Milankovitch cycles and the history of the solar system. PNAS, doi:10.1073/pnas.1717689115 (Xiamaling Formation; uncertainties are 2σ)
sources.lantink2022: Lantink, Davies, Ovtcharova & Hilgen 2022. Milankovitch cycles in banded iron formations constrain the Earth–Moon system 2.46 billion years ago. PNAS 119, e2117146119, doi:10.1073/pnas.2117146119 (Joffre Member; precession constant 108.6 ± 8.5 ″/yr, Earth–Moon distance 321,800 ± 6,500 km, day length 16.9 ± 0.2 h; the ± convention is not stated in the abstract — TimeOptMCMC, Meyers' method, reports 2σ)
sources.nanfen2023: Length of day at c. 1.1 Ga based on cyclostratigraphic analyses of the Nanfen Formation. J. Geol. Soc. 180, doi:10.1144/jgs2022-022 (18.9 ± 0.4 h as read by Zhou 2024; a reanalysis, 'The Orbital Cycle Factory', reads the same spectra as 22.37 ± 0.12 h)

anchors.note: DOCUMENTED −7.2 % (3.6σ), plan 12 option A — THE OPEN DISCREPANCY of falsification leg 1: the composed rate on the cited history misses Zhou 2024's two older Mesoproterozoic constants (here and Wumishan) in the direction of their 'tidal dissipation peak from ~1.3 to 1.5 Ga, indicating a possible unfound resonance' (their words). Farhat 2022's own precession column misses them the same way. Either the ocean-model solution lacks that resonance or the inferred k is biased; the model states the gap and does not fit it. An unexplained improvement fails this gate.
